headline_marked: [[Claude Opus 5.5]] beats GPT-6 Sol in quality, but Sol wins on price
headline: Claude Opus 5.5 beats GPT-6 Sol in quality, but Sol wins on price
summary: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 excels in quality, while OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol offers a significantly lower price-to-performance ratio, sparking a new battleground in the AI market.
details: Two major AI players, Anthropic and OpenAI, simultaneously released new models: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol (with GPT-6 Luna) on September 22, 2026. Initial comparisons reveal a split victory: Opus 5.5 leads in quality, while GPT-6 Sol offers a compelling price advantage.

Direct comparison of benchmark figures is challenging as each company uses different testing environments and benchmarks. However, third-party tests and independent reviews suggest Opus 5.5 generally outperforms GPT-6 Sol in quality metrics. Despite this, GPT-6 Sol is priced approximately 47% lower than Opus 5.5, making it a strong contender for cost-conscious developers.

Anthropic highlights Opus 5.5's real-world value with examples like completing a 680,000-line code migration in a single day and reducing web app load times. They also emphasize its improved communication, being more direct and easier to understand than previous versions.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol, while potentially less capable in raw quality, presents a significant cost-saving opportunity. The price cut is seen as both a competitive move and a way to manage internal costs, as OpenAI notes researchers can spend up to $7,000 daily on tokens. Luna, priced at $0.10 per million tokens, is also noted as a significant development.

User feedback indicates a shift in focus from 'best model' to 'best value model'. Developers are exploring hybrid strategies, using more expensive models for planning and high-level tasks, GPT-6 Sol for execution, Luna for simpler tasks, and then a premium model for final review.

However, GPT-6 Sol's 'improvements' in some benchmarks are attributed to a higher rate of declining to answer, leading to a lower overall accuracy in certain scenarios. Opus 5.5, on the other hand, provides comprehensive documentation and external evaluations, including a System Card and assessments from NIST.

The AI market is evolving, with companies moving beyond simply boasting the highest performance to demonstrating the best return on investment. This new focus on price-to-performance is likely to define the competitive landscape in the coming years.

headline_marked: Anthropic's Claude Code [[skips AGENTS.md]] when telemetry is off
headline: Anthropic's Claude Code skips AGENTS.md when telemetry is off
summary: A user discovered that Claude Code 2.1.277 silently ignores local AGENTS.md files if telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled, requiring a workaround.
details: Claude Code version 2.1.277 introduced support for AGENTS.md files, intended to provide instructions to the AI. However, a user found that this feature is controlled by a remote feature flag and is skipped if telemetry or nonessential network traffic is turned off.

The loader for AGENTS.md functions as a built-in plugin. Its availability is tied to a remote feature flag, 'tengu_agents_md_mod'. If Claude Code cannot fetch this flag, the plugin is considered unavailable, and the local AGENTS.md file is not read, even though reading a markdown file requires no network access.

Testing revealed that when telemetry is disabled, Claude Code silently skips the AGENTS.md file without any warning. This means the model operates without the project-specific instructions contained in the file, potentially leading users to believe the model is ignoring them rather than failing to load the instructions.

This issue affects not only direct users of Claude Code but also those using third-party gateways, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI, as the feature flag resolution fails in these environments as well. Users who disable nonessential traffic by policy are particularly impacted.

The lack of a warning or error message is the most significant problem. Users are left unaware that their instructions are not being processed, leading to wasted time debugging prompts instead of recognizing the file loading failure. This contradicts the expectation that disabling telemetry should only affect diagnostic data, not core functionality.

As a workaround, the user employs a one-line CLAUDE.md file placed alongside AGENTS.md. This file supports '@path' imports and does not depend on the remote flag, allowing the instructions to be loaded even with telemetry disabled. This effectively bypasses the intended AGENTS.md functionality at the cost of an extra file.
